bibliographic.title: PALLM: Evaluating and Enhancing PALLiative Care Conversations with Large Language Models
bibliographic.authors: Zhiyuan Wang, Fangxu Yuan, Virginia LeBaron, Tabor Flickinger, Laura E. Barnes
bibliographic.citation_apa: Wang, Z., Yuan, F., LeBaron, V., Flickinger, T., & Barnes, L. E. (2024). PALLM: Evaluating and enhancing palliative care conversations with large language models. Preprint.

methodology.method_family: experimental LLM evaluation and fine-tuning using clinician-labeled simulated clinical conversation scripts
methodology.study_design: comparative evaluation of proprietary and fine-tuned open-source LLMs on labeled palliative care conversation scripts
methodology.sample_description: simulated scripts crafted and labeled by healthcare professionals; synthetic dataset generated by GPT-4
methodology.technology_context: GPT-4 and fine-tuned LLaMA2 used to evaluate palliative care communication metrics such as understanding, empathy, emotion, and clarity

eligibility.decision_rationale: The study directly addresses LLMs applied to clinical/palliative care conversations in a regulated healthcare setting, but the provided text centers on using LLMs as evaluators of communication quality rather than on governance mechanisms such as guardrails, audit, compliance controls, human oversight, accountability, or operational governance of conversational systems.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and early introduction pages were provided; governance-related content may appear later, and venue/peer-review status remain unclear.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is based only on pages 1-2. The objective and basic method are clear, but sample size, full evaluation protocol, statistical analysis, limitations, and ethics approval are not evidenced in the excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: The excerpt presents a coherent empirical study on LLM-based evaluation of palliative care conversations, but adequacy is limited because dataset size, full methods, and governance implications are not shown in the provided text.

coding.theme: LLM-based evaluation of palliative care communication quality
coding.subtheme: communication metrics for empathy, emotion, and clarity
rq_alignment: operational monitoring of conversational quality in regulated healthcare

synthesis.main_claim: LLMs can evaluate palliative care communication quality and outperform traditional NLP approaches, with GPT-4 and fine-tuned LLaMA2 providing actionable feedback on metrics such as understanding and empathy.
synthesis.contribution: Introduces PALLM as an approach for LLM-empowered assessment of clinical communication, using clinician-labeled simulated scripts and synthetic data to test proprietary and in-house models.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on LLM evaluation of clinical conversations in regulated healthcare; useful for monitoring/quality-assessment angles, but not as primary evidence on conversational governance mechanisms.
